keyDefinitions.name: pc_handshake_at
keyDefinitions.role: The cross-row adjacency predicate, explicitly defined to live OUTSIDE the per-row Clean Component. Closed form: (1 - segment_l1 row) * (pc row - [set_pc(row-1)*(c_0(row-1)+jmp_offset1(row-1)) + (1-set_pc(row-1))*(pc(row-1)+jmp_offset2(row-1)) + flag(row-1)*(jmp_offset1(row-1)-jmp_offset2(row-1))]) = 0. Definitionally identical to v1 pc_handshake (pc_handshake_at_iff_v1, by rfl). Docstring: it 'is a caller-supplied hypothesis' — i.e. a residual, NOT derived from any constraint.

keyDefinitions.name: pc_handshake (v1)
keyDefinitions.role: The legacy named-column closed form of the PIL PC-transition constraint (main.pil:409-410). Same expression as pc_handshake_at. The '-prefix (previous-row rotation) is extractor-rendered as (row := row-1)(rotation := 0), gated by (1 - SEGMENT_L1) so row 0 is vacuous (Nat.sub saturation).

keyDefinitions.name: pc_handshake_with_next_pc
keyDefinitions.role: Next-PC specialization: next_pc = set_pc row*(c_0 row+jmp_offset1 row) + (1-set_pc row)*(pc row+jmp_offset2 row) + flag row*(jmp_offset1 row-jmp_offset2 row). This is the form branches/JAL/JALR actually consume. Derived from pc_handshake at row+1 via pc_handshake_to_next_pc ONLY given a caller witness h_seg : segment_l1(row+1)=0. The next_pc here IS v.pc(row+1) — i.e. the NEXT ROW's pc column.

findings: (1) WHAT THE CROSS-ROW FACT IS. The fact is: pc(row i+1) = decoded-next-pc(row i), where decoded-next-pc(row i) = set_pc(i)*(c_0(i)+jmp_offset1(i)) + (1-set_pc(i))*(pc(i)+jmp_offset2(i)) + flag(i)*(jmp_offset1(i)-jmp_offset2(i)). This is the PIL main.pil:409-410 PC-transition constraint (closed form pc_handshake / pc_handshake_at). The Main row has NO separate nextPC witness column — the 'next PC' is literally the NEXT ROW's pc column. So the fact is intrinsically cross-row: it relates two adjacent rows of the single Main table. For non-jump rows (set_pc=0, flag=0) it specializes to pc(i+1)=pc(i)+jmp_offset2(i)=pc(i)+4 (sequential advance, every opcode); flag=1 gives pc(i)+jmp_offset1=pc(i)+imm (taken branch / JAL).

(2) WHY IT IS NOT DERIVABLE TODAY (two compounding reasons). (a) Single-row Component ceiling: the live Main circuit is circuit : GeneralFormalCircuit with Spec := fun row _ _ => Spec row, packaged as Air.Flat.Component FGL := ⟨circuit⟩ (Circuit.lean:127,175). Air.Flat.Component is per-row: its rowOperations / constraintsHold are evaluated row-by-row, so the Spec literally cannot mention pc(row+1). Spec.lean:43's docstring confirms: the cross-row pc_handshake 'is NOT in this per-row Spec.' Circuit.lean's component docstring confirms: 'Cross-row PC continuity and program semantics remain outside these row-local proofs.' (b) The constraint lives only in the dead model: the PC-transition constraint uses a negative row rotation ('set_pc, 'c[0]); per docs/extraction/extractor-notes.md:373-394 the extractor rewrites row_offset=-1 to (row:=row-1)(rotation:=0). That rendering exists only in the legacy [Circuit F ExtF C] Extraction model / the v1 Valid_Main pc_handshake def — NOT in the live Clean ensemble's trace.constraints (witness.Constraints), which is the per-row Component constraint set. So neither the form of Air.Flat.Component nor the contents of AcceptedTrace.constraints can yield the fact.

(3) HOW IT IS CARRIED AS A RESIDUAL TODAY. Two surfaces, same fact. (i) In the legacy ZiskCircuit / Equivalence path for jumps: pc_handshake_with_next_pc is the LAST conjunct of branch_subset_holds (Main.lean:329) and jump_subset_holds (Main.lean:343); these bundles are CALLER HYPOTHESES of Equivalence.Beq/Bne/Blt/Bge/Bltu/Bgeu, Equivalence.Jal, Equivalence.Jalr and Wrappers/Jal, Wrappers/Jalr (and LoadD/StoreD via pc_handshake_branch). The handshake is obtained by destructuring h_subset (e.g. BranchEqual.lean:83, Jal.lean:94) — never derived. (ii) In the 30 P4-sound constructions: it is the standalone top-level binder h_nextPC_matches : (register_type_pc_equiv ▸ BitVec.ofNat 64 (exec_row[1]!.pc).val) = (PureSpec.execute_<OP>_pure input).nextPC, explicitly labeled '(b)-pending-infra (1)' in ConstructionAdd.lean and present in all 10 Construction*.lean files. It is loaded into the per-op *Promises record's nextPC_matches field and consumed by BusEmission.lean's bus_effect_matches_sail_* lemmas (one per family) to collapse the Sail writeReg Register.nextPC step.

(4) WHICH ARMS NEED IT. Strictly required for control-flow opcodes: BEQ, BNE, BLT, BGE, BLTU, BGEU (6 branches) + JAL + JALR (8 total — the #100 set). But the residual is structurally present on EVERY opcode: even sequential ALU ops carry h_nextPC_matches because every Sail execute writes nextPC = PC+4 and the equality circuit-emitted-pc = Sail-nextPC must be discharged. For the 30 sound P4 arms the fact is the SAME pc(i+1)=pc(i)+4 specialization (flag=0,set_pc=0), so a single cross-row capability that derives pc(i+1)=decoded-next-pc(i) discharges h_nextPC_matches uniformly across all 63 opcodes, with branches/JAL/JALR being the cases where decoded-next-pc is non-trivial (imm/computed target).

(5) WHAT A CROSS-ROW CAPABILITY MUST PRODUCE. It must DERIVE, from witness.BalancedChannels (the proof-system trust class already in AcceptedTrace.balanced), the adjacency equation pc(row i+1) = decoded-next-pc(row i) for arbitrary i in a multi-row Main table — i.e. produce pc_handshake_at trace.mainTable (i+1) (equivalently pc_handshake_with_next_pc at row i with next_pc = pc(i+1)), then bridge pc(i+1) to the execution-bus exec_row[1]!.pc cell so it yields exactly the h_nextPC_matches RHS = Sail nextPC. Concretely it must (a) introduce a Main-row→Main-row continuity channel (the PC handshake) as an OrderedChannel/addChannel-style member of the SAME balanced interaction list — a VERIFIER ENDPOINT, mirroring how #103's SeamTagChain models the boot push at tag 0 and the per-row push=pull+1 emission; (b) prove the per-adjacent-row relation is forced by global balance for general N (not just one row), avoiding the route-b VACUITY trap where the seam only balances on degenerate single-row traces; (c) NOT relocate the fact into a new caller premise or a fresh axiom (anti-laundering). The deliverable downstream is the elimination of h_nextPC_matches as a binder from the 30 constructions and the elimination of pc_handshake_with_next_pc from branch_subset_holds/jump_subset_holds.

map.routeVerdict: Not a route-probe reader; the addChannel-vs-addVm verdict for #100 is UNRESOLVED and is itself the first open question this map surfaces. Evidence both ways: (FOR addVm) the existing GO spike (spike-a-xrow, Spike/CrossRowVm.lean) already derived row1.pc=row0.pc+4 from a VM global balance, sorry-free, 0 PROJECT axioms — feasibility is demonstrated on the addVm route. (AGAINST addVm) it was condemned for #103 because 'a VM table cannot also PROVIDE a finished channel, and Mem must push the finished MemBus'; the #103 supersede banner states #100 most likely also wants addChannel. CRUX: #103's blocker is specific to Mem PROVIDING the finished MemBus — the analogous question for #100 is whether the cross-row PC continuity channel must PROVIDE a finished channel. If the PC handshake is a pure adjacency relation (Main row i+1 consumes what Main row i pushes, with no obligation to also provide a finished external channel), the #103 doubly-blocked condition does NOT obviously apply and addVm may be legitimately reusable; if the live Main op-bus emission entangles the PC continuity with a provided channel, #100 inherits the same block and must use the OrderedChannel/addChannel idiom (SeamTagChain template). RECOMMENDATION: resolve empirically by re-examining the spike-a-xrow VM against the 'must-provide-finished-channel' criterion before committing the route.

ADDCHANNEL for #100. The addVm route (Spike A) is sound only in a standalone empty ensemble; it CANNOT be used to make the PRODUCTION Main a VM table, because it hits the exact same blocker (1) that doubly-blocked addVm for #103. addChannel is the route; the SeamTagChain engine already generalizes to it.

MECHANISM (the make-or-break reasoning):
(a) Does the cross-row PC handshake table need to PROVIDE (finish) a channel? NO — and that is not even the blocker. The blocker is the MIRROR: the production Main table already REQUIRES two FINISHED channels. `componentWithRomMemAndOpBus` (origin/main:ZiskFv/AirsClean/Main/Constraints.lean:440) sets `channelsWithRequirements := [MemBusChannel.toRaw, OpBusChannel.toRaw]` and `channelsWithGuarantees := []` — Main is a pure CONSUMER that `.emit`s (assumeGuarantees:=false ⇒ requirements) both OpBus and MemBus, which `fullRv64imEnsemble` (origin/main:ZiskFv/AirsClean/FullEnsemble.lean:124-125) closes via `.addFinishedChannel OpBusChannel`/`MemBusChannel`. The addVm builder `SoundEnsemble.addVm` requires `reqs_disjoint_finished : ∀ channel ∈ ens.finished, ... ∀ table ∈ vm.tables, channel ∉ table.circuit.channelsWithRequirements` (Vm.lean:688). Making Main a VM table puts OpBus AND MemBus (both finished) in a VM table's requirements ⇒ `reqs_disjoint_finished` is FALSE. This is blocker (1) verbatim, the same one that killed addVm for #103's Mem rows (which required the finished MemBus). So addVm is doubly suspect for production #100 too.

(b) Can a SeamTagChain-style addChannel derivation force pc_(i+1)=nextpc(pc_i) from balance? YES, by the IDENTICAL idiom #103 landed. Add a NEW PC-continuation channel `PcContChannel` (Guarantees := True), and have the Main row EMIT (not pull/push) a per-row pair: `PcContChannel.emit (-1) (prevPcTagged row_index)` and `PcContChannel.emit (gate) (nextPcTagged (row_index+1))`, plus a boot endpoint table that `.emit 1 (bootPc tag 0)` — EXACTLY mirroring the landed #103 `componentWithDualMemBus` (origin/p4-103-landing:ZiskFv/AirsClean/Mem/Circuit.lean:272-280 `SeamContChannel.emit (-1)` / `emit (1 - is_last_segment)` and bootComp:336 `SeamContChannel.emit 1`). Using `.emit` keeps `channelsWithGuarantees := []` so the channel escapes `SoundEnsemble.subset_finished` (it lives only in channelsWithRequirements). Add it via `SoundEnsemble.addChannel` (OrderedChannel.lean:683 — joins ens.channels with NO soundness obligation, no OrderedChannel/Consistent burden). Its balance becomes a conjunct of `BalancedChannels` (FlatEnsemble.lean:336). Then the existing general-N engine `SeamTagChain.boot_chain_derived_generalN` (origin/p4-103-landing:ZiskFv/Channels/SeamTagChain.lean; weighted-balance `weightedSum_eq_zero_of_balance` + Newton-tag-forcing + `exists_push_of_pull` push-classification) forces, per tag k, that the tag-k pull value equals the unique tag-k push value — i.e. row(i+1).prevPc = row(i).nextPc. With the row-local pin nextPc = f(pc) (the constraint_18 multiplexer; for sequential rows = pc+4) this yields the cross-row PC chain. NOTHING relocates the fact into a caller premise or axiom: it is a conjunct of BalancedChannels (the existing channel-balance trust class), exactly as #103.

(c) Was Spike A's addVm GO actually sound? Sound AS A STANDALONE PoC (it is sorry-free, kernel-only, non-vacuous), but it INHERITS THE FLAW for production use: it dodged the doubly-blocked obstruction only because it built on `SoundEnsemble.empty` with NO finished OpBus/MemBus. The moment Main's real OpBus/MemBus requirements are present (the production ensemble), addVm's `reqs_disjoint_finished` fails. So Spike A's GO does NOT transfer to production #100. (Its SoundVmEnsemble cycle math — deriving pc=4*step from `guarantees_of_requirements_of_requirements_of_guarantees` — is correct and is genuinely a different derivation engine than SeamTagChain's `exists_push_of_pull`, but the carrying vehicle is unusable in production.)

FIRST CONSTRUCTION TO ATTEMPT: a non-vacuous channel-level PoC paralleling #103's `SeamNonVacuity`/`boot_chain_derived`. Define a `PcContChannel : Channel FGL (fields M)` carrying `(pc, tag)` (and any needed mux selectors) with Guarantees:=True; reuse `SeamTagChain.bootList2`/`bootChainN` verbatim (it is channel-agnostic) to get `boot_chain_derived` forcing row(i+1).pulledPc-tuple = row(i).pushedPc-tuple from a balanced boot+2-row interaction list; then exhibit a concrete BALANCED 2-row witness (boot tag0; row0 pull boot / push pc+4 tag1; row1 pull (pc+4) tag1 / gated-off push) and run the derivation to land row1.pc = row0.pc + 4 NON-vacuously. That is the cheap GO/NO-GO. The deeper production wiring then mirrors #103's L2-L5: add the is_first_row/row-index column + emit on Main + `.addChannel PcContChannel` on the real ensemble + airval-to-column bridge + discharge the next-PC residual `h_nextPC_matches`.
